claims.statement: Tom Allen lost to Joe Goss on an intentional foul in the 21st round on September 7, 1876, in Boone County, Kentucky, for a $2,000 a side stake.
claims.excerpt: The mill went 21 rounds and Alen lost on an intenttonal foul.

claims.statement: Both Allen and Goss were arrested after the fight; Allen got out on bail and fled to England.
claims.excerpt: Both men were arrested, but Alien. after getting cut on ball, fled to England.

claims.statement: After returning to America, Allen settled in St. Louis.

claims.statement: Allen ran a saloon known as the Champion Rest in St. Louis until a few weeks before his death.

fights.excerpt: The mill went 21 rounds and Alen lost on an intenttonal foul.
fights.notes: Allen lost on an intentional foul after striking Goss while he was down; Goss was given the decision. Stopped by militia in Kenton County and moved to Boone County.

notes: Written in 1903, looking back at 1876. The article says Goss was declared champion of America. Hint's 'near Cincinnati' is not in the text.
